question: Does a SEQUENCE of consecutive frames tell a vision-language model more about 'is this person speaking' than a SINGLE frame does? The control is the same frames in a scrambled order, which keeps appearance and destroys motion.
hypothesis: A single frame cannot show motion, and the question asked of the model is about movement ('their mouth is moving'). So the published +0.4545 margin may be reading a single frame's mouth-open cue rather than motion. If it is reading motion, then an ORDERED strip of consecutive frames must beat the SAME frames in a SHUFFLED order.
headline_definition: per model and per K: margin_over_silent(strip) - margin_over_silent(strip_shuffled), where margin_over_silent = sensitivity_on_speak - fpr_on_silent_person_present. Reported alongside the FPRs so it can be checked that the two strips ran at a matched false-positive rate.
question_text: Is the person in this image SPEAKING (their mouth is moving or open, as if talking) or NOT SPEAKING (mouth closed, still)? Answer with exactly one word: SPEAKING or NOT SPEAKING.

request_shape.pacing_note: The scheduler's per-model call interval at the end of the run, for the record. A rate-limit error doubles a model's interval and a success walks it back down; the interval is a scheduling detail and changes no stimulus and no answer.
request_shape.png_encoder: experiments/cloud_multimodal.write_png -- greyscale (colour type 0), 8 bits per pixel

image_construction.layout: horizontal strips: tiles side by side, TIME RUNS LEFT TO RIGHT. The grid arm: 2x2, ROW-MAJOR, so time runs left to right and then wraps to the next row.
image_construction.upscale_note: Each TILE is upscaled by its stimulus's `scale` before tiling. Bilinear is a weighted sum of neighbouring REAL source pixels, so an upscaled tile carries exactly the information of the original frame and adds no structure that was not there. That is what makes `single_up` a test of RESOLUTION rather than of added detail.
image_construction.strip_definition: K CONSECUTIVE frames of one session, in time order, tiled into one image. The K=4 window is the first 4 frames of the K=8 window, so the two K arms are nested.
image_construction.shuffle_definition: the same K frames in a permuted order. The identity and every cyclic rotation are rejected, because a rotation preserves k-1 of the k adjacencies and so is not a motion-destroyed control.
image_construction.repeat_definition: K copies of ONE frame from that moment: the same pixel content k times, no temporal information at all.
confounds: `strip_k8` has TWICE the total pixels of `strip_k4` (2560x192 vs 1280x192) because the tiles are tiled, so the K comparison is confounded with total image area. The HEADLINE comparison (strip vs strip_shuffled at the SAME K) has identical dimensions and identical pixels, so it is free of this.

`single_up` (640x384) and `grid_k4` (640x384) have the SAME dimensions and the SAME total pixel count, 245760, so those two differ only in arrangement and multiplicity: one big frame against four frames in a 2x2 grid.

`strip_k4` (1280x192) is 6.67:1. Llama 3.2 Vision has no multi-image interface -- it tiles ONE image -- so a wide strip arrives as a wide band divided into arbitrary crops. The `grid_k4` arm exists to separate 'the frames do not help' from 'the 6.67:1 shape does not help'.

frame_geometry.measurement_stride_why: These captures are written by /mnt/c/proart_capture/nv12small.py as Y (15360) + U plane (1920) + V plane (1920) = 19200 bytes per frame, PLANAR chroma, not the interleaved 4:2:0 that W*H*3//2 = 23040 assumes. 19200 x 900 = 17280000 = the exact file size, and 900 frames at 30.02 fps matches the 29.981 s WAV.
frame_geometry.control_stride_why: The standard 4:2:0 stride every reader in this repo used. Read at this stride the same files yield 750 frames and 80% of them are TORN: rows from frame k mixed with rows from frame k+1. The `*_torn` stimuli are built from that read, and are a CONTROL, never a measurement.
frame_geometry.mean_abs_consecutive_diff_note: The identity of a frame set. A real 30 fps webcam scene changes by a fraction of a grey level between consecutive frames; a torn read changes by tens of grey levels and by the SAME amount in every session, because it measures the tear and not the scene.

speak.selection_rule: anchors are the middles of DETECTED-SPEECH runs long enough to contain the whole K=8 window, thinned evenly over the session; the label of every frame in the window comes from the gate on the WAV at that frame's own timestamp

silent.selection_rule: anchors spread evenly over the session (first second skipped for encoder warm-up); the gate on the WAV detects NO speech anywhere in this session, so every frame of every window is a no-speech frame

turned.selection_rule: the TURNED condition: head turned away, speaking; anchors chosen by the same rule as `speak`, from DETECTED-SPEECH runs on the turned session's WAV. Reported separately and NEVER pooled with `speak`.

blank.selection_rule: K copies of one uniform 128 grey frame; run at the same count as the real conditions so the denominators stay equal

denominators.note: Every condition is scored with the SAME number of stimuli, so every rate has the same denominator. The blank condition's stimuli are byte-identical to each other, so its rate is a per-call rate on ONE image; it is run at the full count to keep the denominators equal, as `cloud_multimodal.py` did.

always_SPEAKING.note: a model that answers SPEAKING to everything, including the blank; scores FPR 1.000

always_NOT_SPEAKING.note: a model that answers NOT SPEAKING to everything; scores sensitivity 0.000 and FPR 0.000

base_rate_note: The published sensitivity of 0.4545 must be read against a constant-answer baseline, NOT against 0. `always_NOT_SPEAKING` has sensitivity 0.000 and `always_SPEAKING` has sensitivity 1.000; both score a margin of exactly 0.000. A margin is the only number here that a constant answer cannot fake.

limits: one session per condition, one speaker, one room, one lighting state
12 moments per condition and frames from one session are correlated, so the effective sample size is far below the frame count; the resolution of a rate is one divided by the denominator
the speech labels come from the Silero gate applied to the WAV; per AV-SYNC.md A.wav and A.nv12 do not correspond, so the per-frame labels are provisional

the model's own internal image resizing is not observable from here, so what the model actually sees after resizing is unknown; the ORDER of the tiles survives any whole-image resize, which is why the shuffled control is valid and the resolution question is not settled by it
one measurement of one model on one capture is one measurement, not a property
